title: The Ark of the Fringe
logline: A rogue ecologist attempts to transport breeding stock of an endangered zero-g silkworm across three star systems to establish a sanctuary, hunted by synthetic polymer corporations determined to protect their patent monopoly.

roles.description: Spent three decades adapting silkworms to produce radiation-shielding thread; visionary, stubborn, refusing to let the species be exterminated.
Enforcement director for the synthetic polymer trust; elegant, ruthless, protecting multi-billion-credit petroleum shielding contracts.
A heavy corporate cruiser patrolling jump gates to seize un-patented biological manufacturing stock.
The underground network of frontier station gardeners and independent bio-engineers.
The chemical manufacturing monopoly holding exclusive military and civilian hull-shielding contracts.
A clandestine hydroponic nursery hidden in the shadow of a hollowed moon in the home system.
An abandoned orbital laboratory in a neighbouring system equipped with zero-g incubation chambers.
An unmapped asteroid haven two jumps away where the silkworms can multiply without corporate interference.

public_situation: Corporate enforcement marshals raid un-patented bio-domes across three star systems, seizing all living specimens of orbital textile organisms.
private_truth: {role:synthetic_trust} declared the radiation-shielding silkworms an invasive hazard because the organic silk offers three times the protection of their synthetic plating at one-tenth the cost.

beats.public_change: Corporate gunboats surround {role:seed_nursery}, preparing to vent the greenhouse modules with industrial pesticides.

missions.reason: She needs an outside pilot to extract three pressurized brood canisters of dormant zero-g silkworm cocoons before the extermination gas is released.
missions.private_fact: She originally developed the silkworm genome while working on corporate grant money and stole the breeding line when they ordered it shredded.

beats.public_change: Patrol craft in the neighboring system deploy biological sensors at the jump gate, scanning all passing freighters for live organic heat signatures.

missions.reason: She hires an outsider to navigate into the border system and download diagnostic telemetry directly from the nursery relay lab, confirming the thermal beds are stable.
missions.private_fact: The silkworm larvae will perish within twelve hours if incubator humidity falls below eighty percent.

beats.public_change: Corporate hunter packs intercept the relay platform, deploying pesticide drones into the habitat intake ducts.

missions.reason: She needs the corporate exterminator drones destroyed immediately before their toxic spray breaches the larval incubation chambers.
missions.private_fact: Her own daughter is among the conservation volunteers defending the relay lab from the interior.

beats.public_change: The silkworms hatch into active feeding larvae, requiring emergency nutrient paste to survive the final jump leg.

missions.reason: She needs specialized organic mulberry leaf slurry purchased from open commercial ports and brought to the sanctuary to sustain the caterpillars.
missions.private_fact: She spent her entire lifetime pension and family savings to purchase the specialized feed.

beats.public_change: {role:patent_interdictor} positions across the sanctuary approach lanes, charging pulse batteries to interdict the transport.

missions.reason: She needs the corporate cruiser disabled so the ark transport can slip into the unmapped asteroid haven and establish the colony.
missions.private_fact: The corporate commander hails mid-combat offering a lifetime patent royalty annuity to incinerate the silkworm canisters on the spot.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot disables the cruiser and delivers the silkworms to the sanctuary.
resolutions.summary: The silkworm breeding colony takes root in {role:sanctuary_belt}. Cheap biological radiation shielding reaches frontier miners, shattering {role:synthetic_trust}'s monopoly.

consequences.public_summary: A mercenary broke through corporate interdictors to carry the last zero-g silkworms across three star systems to a secret asteroid haven.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot accepts the corporate royalty deal and surrenders the cocoons.
resolutions.summary: {role:synthetic_trust} locks the silkworms into proprietary corporate bio-vaults. Shielding prices remain extortionate, and {role:renegade_ecologist} is imprisoned for intellectual property theft.

consequences.public_summary: Dark rumors tell of a courier who traded an endangered species of living radiation-shielding silkworms to a chemical monopoly for a patent royalty.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot fails the mission lines or the larvae perish.
resolutions.summary: The last breeding stock of orbital silkworms is wiped out. {role:synthetic_trust} retains absolute control over radiation shielding, and frontier miners continue paying exorbitant costs.

loose_threads.detail: The regional exchange reports an eight-hundred percent profit margin on synthetic polymer shielding sold to civilian transport fleets.
The municipal bio-hazard clearance warrant classifying the silkworms as lethal vermin was signed by a director holding stock in the polymer trust.
The hull armor on {role:patent_interdictor} bears repainted insignias from a private mercenary army contracted by the chemical cartel.

radio_hooks: Synthetic polymer trust warns against uncertified biological materials aboard frontier vessels.
Miners report rising hull degradation as official radiation shielding prices climb.
Ecological activists accuse chemical manufacturers of waging corporate war against nature.

voice_direction.renegade_ecologist: Fierce, articulate, and fiercely defiant. Speaks of her adapted silkworms with the tender reverence of a mother defending endangered infants, brushing off corporate lawsuits with cold scorn.
voice_direction.patent_director: Silky, aristocratic, and coldly transactional. Treats the extinction of a unique species as an unavoidable legal requirement for patent protection.
